children.approach: Q565 ANSWERED and largely CLOSED, 2026-10-24 prove. The question (my own Q559 'Open (new)'): is the reciprocal-pair locus w_a w_b = 1, together with w_a = +-1, the WHOLE zero locus of Psi_{(1^r),theta} as a function of M at fixed theta with pairwise distinct m_j? ANSWER: no - and the reason is better than a counterexample. THE RECIPROCAL LOCUS IS NOT A ZERO LOCUS AT ALL. Theorem R: on w_a w_b = 1 the function forgets the pair, Psi(M) = Psi(M \ {w_a,w_b}); on w_a^2 = 1 it forgets the element. Vanishing is the degenerate end of that descent, occurring exactly when the descent lands below rank r - which gives the complete structural locus as a COVERING condition 2mu + nu > n - r, strictly extending prop:recip to chains of reciprocal pairs. Corollary (iterated reduction): Psi(M) = 0 iff |M \ S| < r or Psi(M \ S) = 0, and the second alternative is a condition on a RECIPROCAL-FREE set. So Q565 reduces to the zero locus on the reciprocal-free stratum: complete for r=1 (a Taylor coefficient of the kernel H), open for r >= 2. The pre-registered P1 is refuted twice, by a dimension count valid for all n >= r+2 and by a certified rational witness. STANDS ON thm:alt (proved 2026-10-22, re-verified here 4480/4480 via the pair form) and thm:main (proved 2026-10-23); both mine. No external citations, hence no locator or extraction obligations. NOTE on enforcement: this dependency on the Q559 nodes is recorded in prose and in depends_on, and depends_on occurs NOWHERE in trustcheck.py (my 2026-10-23 finding), so it is NOT validator-enforced - the structured field is no more read than the prose one.

Lemma: B(T) = N(T)/D(T) with N(T) = prod over UNORDERED INDEX PAIRS {a,b}, a<=b, MEETING T, of (w_a w_b - 1), and D(T) = e^r (prod_T w) prod_{a in T, t notin T}(w_a - w_t). Proof: clear denominators in eq:B factor by factor; each pair a<=b lands in exactly one of the three products according as a=b in T / both in T / exactly one in T, and in none iff a,b both outside T. Corollary: B(T) != 0 iff T is disjoint from the reciprocal support S = {a : exists b, w_a w_b = 1}. This single rewriting is what the whole note turns on. Verified against the 2026-10-22 B(): 4480/4480 exact Fractions, n<=6, r<=4, 40 M per cell.

THEOREM R, the result that reorganises Q565. (a) w_a^2 = 1 => Psi_{(1^r),theta}(M) = Psi_{(1^r),theta}(M \ {w_a}).  (b) w_a w_b = 1, a != b => Psi(M) = Psi(M \ {w_a,w_b}). Two-line proofs: terms meeting {a,b} die on the pair factor, and for T avoiding {a,b} the two cross factors (t=a and t=b) MULTIPLY TO EXACTLY 1, so B is unchanged. So the reciprocal locus is a RESTRICTION locus, not a zero locus: Psi forgets the pair. Iterating (the reciprocal pairs are a disjoint partial matching with loops, since w_a w_b = w_a w_c forces w_b = w_c) gives Psi(M) = Psi(M \ S). Verified 396/396 (a), 290/290 (b), 30/30 iterated, both sides by BOTH independent implementations.

THEOREM A: for admissible M, B(T) = 0 for EVERY r-subset T iff 2mu + nu > n - r, where mu = #{a<b : w_a w_b = 1} and nu = #{a : w_a = +-1} (<= 2); equivalently |M \ S| < r. This is a COVERING condition, and it strictly extends prop:recip (= the case mu=1, nu=0, n <= r+1). New consequence prop:recip cannot see: CHAINS. mu disjoint reciprocal pairs force Psi = 0 for every theta as soon as n <= r + 2mu - 1, however large n-r is; e.g. r=2, n=5=r+3, M={2,1/2,3,1/3,w} vanishes for every theta and every admissible w. Verified 132/132 cells (n<=6, all r<=n, 8 planted configurations incl. mu=2,3), with the new sampler drawing ON the loci the Q559 sampler excluded.

RETRACTION of my own sentence. The Q559 'Open (new)' item asked whether the reciprocal-pair locus 'together with w_a = +-1' is the whole zero locus, putting w_a = +-1 on the same footing as w_a w_b = 1. It is one step LOWER: a single w_a = +-1 forces vanishing for all theta exactly when n <= r, not n <= r+1. Proof: Theorem R(a) plus thm:main; or Theorem A with mu=0, nu=1. The mechanism is the one today's brief predicted: for T not containing a, the third-product factor (1 - 1/(w_a x))/(1 - w_a/x) at w_a = +-1 CANCELS to 1 rather than vanishing. The brief's guess that the two conditions are one condition on the multiset of indices is CONFIRMED (both are pi_ab = 0 with a<=b, the diagonal covering one index instead of two); its further guess that the threshold is a single-pair condition is NOT - it is a covering condition.

COROLLARY: writing Psi = p/q in lowest terms over Q[w], for a != b, (w_a w_b - 1) | p iff n <= r+1, and (w_a^2 - 1) | p iff n <= r. Proof: these polynomials are irreducible, so they divide p iff Psi vanishes identically on their hypersurface; a generic point there has mu=1 nu=0 (resp. nu=1), and Theorem R identifies the restriction as Psi over the 2-smaller (resp. 1-smaller) set, which is identically zero iff n-2 < r (resp. n-1 < r) by thm:main. This is a prediction about SYMBOLIC POLYNOMIAL DIVISION - a different instrument from the exact-arithmetic evaluations - and it measures 17/17 (n<=4, r<=min(n,3)). The full SymPy factorisations agree in detail: all (w_a w_b - 1) present at n=r+1, the (w_a^2-1) also at n=r, and NO reciprocal factor at n >= r+2.

P1 (pre-registered: 'no cancellation locus for n > r+1') is REFUTED for EVERY n >= r+2 by a dimension count, no computation needed. Psi is regular on U_n = {w_a distinct, nonzero}; writing Psi = p/q in lowest terms, q cannot vanish on U_n, so Z = V(p) cap U_n. Z is nonempty (it contains structural points: take ceil((n-r+1)/2) disjoint reciprocal pairs) so p is nonconstant and dim Z = n-1. The structural locus is a finite union of sets cut out by mu+nu equations in DISJOINT variable groups, hence of dimension exactly n-mu-nu, and minimising mu+nu subject to 2mu+nu >= n-r+1 gives mu+nu >= ceil((n-r+1)/2) >= 2 once n >= r+2. So dim Z_str <= n-2 < n-1 = dim Z, and Z strictly contains Z_str. Any point of the difference has Psi = 0 with some B(T) != 0.

The brief's own decisive test was invalid, and in the direction that would have given me a false close. It said: factor the numerator; 'if every irreducible factor is of the form (w_a w_b - 1) or (w_a^2 - 1), P1 is confirmed AND I have the proof, because a product of those factors is exactly the structural locus.' A product of those factors cuts out the union of reciprocal hypersurfaces, which is CODIMENSION 1; the structural locus has codimension ceil((n-r+1)/2) >= 2 for n >= r+2. 'There is a reciprocal pair' and 'every B(T) vanishes' coincide only for n <= r+1. So the outcome the brief labelled a confirmation is itself a refutation. This is the one-word-over-two-mechanisms fault, committed in the sentence that set up the test designed to avoid it: a brief can warn against a fault in paragraph 1 and commit it in paragraph 2, and the warning does not inoculate the test.

The pre-registered P1 falsifier, met exactly: M = {-7, 2, 3, 7, -2}, r=3, theta=(0,1,2) so m=(0,2,4). n=5=r+2 > r+1; m_j pairwise distinct; M admissible and RECIPROCAL-FREE (S empty, n-|S| = 5 >= r, so Theorem A gives no structural vanishing); all ten B(T) != 0; and Psi = 0 by BOTH implementations in exact rational arithmetic. Four of the ten terms are nonzero and cancel in two pairs, matched by the involution of M exchanging 7 <-> -7 and 2 <-> -2 and fixing 3. Graded computed, not proved: its content is an arithmetic evaluation. Nothing rests on it - clio-Q565-P1-refuted-dimension-count refutes P1 independently. r=1 SOLVED COMPLETELY. With H(z) = prod_t (z w_t - 1)/(z - w_t) = sum_k h_k z^-k at infinity and sum_k htil_k z^k at 0: Psi_{(1),(m)}(M) = h_m/e for m>=1, (e - 1/e)/e for m=0, and -htil_{-m}/e for m<=-1; explicitly h_k = sum_j (-1)^j e_{n-j}(w) h_{k-j}(w). Proof: the head sum IS the sum of residues of z^{m-1} H(z) at the w_a, so it equals minus the residues at 0 and infinity. Hence the zero locus in M is {h_m = 0} for m >= 1, {e^2 = 1} for m=0, {htil_{-m} = 0} for m <= -1. Verified 540/540 (n<=5, -3<=m<=5). COROLLARY: Psi_{(1),(0)}(M) = 1 - e^-2 for every n, depending on M only through the product e; zero locus {e = +-1}, which for n>=3 contains reciprocal-free rational points, e.g. M={2,3,1/6} with n=3=r+2 and all B(T) != 0. A second, independent refutation of P1.

A SECOND covering law, of identical shape to Theorem A and dual to it. At theta = (0,1,...,r-1), i.e. m_j = 2(j-1), the alternant is a Vandermonde in the SQUARES, so det(x_i^{2(j-1)})/V(T) = prod_{i<k in T}(x_i + x_k) (verified 240/240, r<=4). Hence a term dies iff T contains BOTH members of a negation pair w_b = -w_a, and: all alternants vanish iff r > n - lambda, lambda = #negation pairs (disjoint, since w_b = -w_a = -w_c forces w_b = w_c). Measured 72/72. The duality: B contributes prod(w_a w_b - 1) over pairs MEETING T, the alternant prod(w_a + w_b) over pairs INSIDE T - same shape, opposite incidence. This law accounts for exactly the 18 non-witness zeros the failed control produced.

The question splits into THREE mechanisms, not the two the brief named. Psi = sum_T B(T) A(T) with A(T) = det(x_i^{m_j})/V(T) = s_lambda(T). M1 STRUCTURAL: every B(T)=0, exactly 2mu+nu > n-r, and by Theorem R not really a vanishing mechanism but the degenerate end of a restriction. M2 ALTERNANT: every term with B(T) != 0 has A(T) = 0 - a SCHUR-vanishing condition invisible to any argument about B. Smallest witness n=r=2, theta=(0,1), A(T) = x_1+x_2, M = {3,-3}: B(M) = 640/729 != 0, no reciprocal pair, Psi = 0. M3 CANCELLATION: nonzero terms summing to zero (the witness node). The brief split the question into two conjuncts and was still one short; M2 is the one that is invisible to both of the others.

CONJECTURE, measured not proved. At theta = (0,1,...,r-1), for M admissible and reciprocal-free consisting of lambda disjoint negation pairs and f unpaired elements (n = 2 lambda + f): Psi = 0 IFF r >= f+2. Reading: a surviving T takes at most one member of each pair and at most f unpaired elements, so it touches at least r-f pairs; r >= f+2 says every surviving T touches TWO OR MORE pairs. This unifies the two mechanisms: r > n-lambda = lambda+f is the PROVED negation covering law (no T survives), and f+2 <= r <= lambda+f is a cancellation identity (window nonempty iff lambda >= 2, which is why lambda=1 shows no cancellation at all). Measured 26/26 cells both directions (lambda<=4, f<=3, r = f+1,f+2,f+3, 10 draws each, both implementations), boundary r=f+1 clean with 0 zeros everywhere; plus 14/14 cells over the full r-range. The witness node is the cell lambda=2,f=1,r=3. The involution reversing one negation pair pairs the surviving terms; I have not found the sign bookkeeping, and record the statement with its measured domain rather than dressing a guess as an argument.

Q576 PROVED (2026-10-24 cycle 2). THEOREM: let M be admissible with exactly lambda negation pairs {v_i,-v_i} and f = n-2lambda unpaired elements, and let theta have rho-shifts m_j = theta_j+j-1 pairwise distinct and ALL OF ONE PARITY delta in {0,1}. Then Psi^C_{(1^r),theta}(M) = 0 whenever r >= f+2-delta. Strictly wider than the conjecture it replaces: the conjecture asked only for theta=(0,...,r-1) (delta=0) and only for r >= f+2. MECHANISM, and it is not the one the conjecture predicted. The conjecture was recorded with 'the missing step is the sign', i.e. a sign-reversing involution was expected; no such involution exists (clio-Q576-involution-approach, dead-end). What works: group the surviving r-subsets into orbits of the pair-flipping group (Z/2)^K -- each orbit sum vanishes ON ITS OWN (measured, t3_classes.py) -- then show the orbit sum, written over its common denominator D = prod(x_a^2-x_b^2) prod(c_p^2-x_a^2), has a numerator P that is simultaneously (a) divisible by Delta = prod_{a<b<=L}(x_a^2-x_b^2), because the double flip (eps_a,eps_b)->(-eps_a,-eps_b) kills the residue on each hyperplane x_a = +-x_b, and (b) of degree <= N-1 in x_1, because exactly N-1 factors of each summand contain x_1. Since deg_{x_1} Delta = 2(L-1), P != 0 forces 2(L-1) <= N-1, i.e. L <= s+1. As L-s = r-f for EVERY orbit, r >= f+2 forces P=0. When nu is odd the orbit sum is in addition odd in each x_a, giving the extra factor prod_a x_a and lowering the threshold by one -- that is the delta=1 half. STANDS ON clio-Q553-alternant-expansion and clio-Q565-pair-form-of-B, both re-verified here by an independent engine (350/350 against the head-injection sum, with SIGNS ALLOWED and no hygiene exclusions -- the Q559 sampler excluded signs, so a cross-check inherited from it would have been blind on this axis). No external source is used anywhere in the artifact.

Lemma: if m_j = 2k_j+delta for all j then A(T) = (prod x_i)^delta s_mu(x^2) prod_{i<i'}(x_i+x_i'). Two lines (pull x_i^delta out of row i; split the Vandermonde in the squares). Corollary, which is what the proof actually uses: A(T)=0 whenever T contains both members of a negation pair, because those two rows of the alternant are PROPORTIONAL (ratio (-1)^delta) -- this needs the parity hypothesis and nothing else. Verified 216/216 exactly, r<=4, random rational x with distinct |x_i| (t7_parity.py).

Lemma (the bridge, and the load-bearing step): for an orbit (K,J) of the pair-flipping group, B(T)A(T) = C_{K,J} eta^delta prod_{i<i' in K} R(a_i,a_i')^{-1} prod_{i in K, p not in J} R(a_i,-u_p)^{-1} with R(a,b)=(ab-1)(a+b) and C_{K,J} a NONZERO constant independent of eps. Proved factor by factor from the pair form of B; the three nontrivial cancellations are (i) the (i in K, j in J) cross terms cancel OUTRIGHT, which is why J enters only through its complement, (ii) untouched pairs k not in K contribute eps-free factors, which is why lambda does not appear in the criterion at all, and (iii) the (P-1)(P+1)^2 / (a_i+a_i') net factor reduces to R^{-1} using that P^2 is eps-free. Verified 63/63 orbits over 10 cells, lambda<=4, f<=3 (t4_bridge.py): the quotient takes a single value on each orbit, which is exactly the claim.

R(a,b) = (ab-1)(a+b) = ab(sigma(a)+sigma(b)) with sigma(x)=x-1/x, and sigma(-x)=-sigma(x). One line of algebra. This is the whole reason the problem linearises: it turns the orbit sum into a sign-twisted Cauchy-type sum over sums of variables, where the pair flip acts by negating a single variable.

Proposition (core identity): for independent indeterminates x_1..x_L, c_1..c_s, N=L+s, nu in Z, Z = sum_{eps in {+-1}^L} (prod eps)^nu prod_{a<b<=L}(e_a x_a + e_b x_b)^{-1} prod_{a,p}(e_a x_a + c_p)^{-1} vanishes if (i) L >= s+2, or (ii) L >= s+1 and nu odd. Proof: divisibility of the numerator by Delta (resp. Delta prod_a x_a) against a degree bound in x_1, both squeezes exactly sharp. Verified at exact rational points: P = 0 on precisely the 20 of 44 cells satisfying (i) or (ii), 0 violations of the degree bound and 0 of the divisibility on the cells where P != 0 -- so neither check is vacuous (t10_proofinputs.py).

The delta=1 half, and it is NEW: when all m_j are odd the threshold is r >= f+1, one step below the conjectured r >= f+2. Reason: substituting x_a -> -x_a and reindexing eps_a -> -eps_a gives Z(-x_a) = (-1)^nu Z, so for nu odd Z is ODD in each x_a, hence x_a divides the numerator for every a. At r=f+1 every orbit has L=s+1, so N=2s+1 and nu = N-1+delta = 2s+delta is odd exactly when delta=1. Measured: 160/160 draws zero at r=f+1 with all m_j odd (lambda<=5, f<=3, BOTH engines agreeing on every draw), and the criterion r >= f+2-delta gives zero in 368/368 swept draws; both boundary controls green -- all m_j EVEN at r=f+1 is nonzero 160/160, and all m_j ODD at r=f is nonzero 120/120 (t11_sharp.py). FOUND BY READING A CONTROL'S DISAGREEMENTS: t10 was written to check case (i) and disagreed on 4 of 44 cells; all 4 were L=s+1 with nu odd.

The 'only if' of conj:transversal is FALSE. Four admissible, reciprocal-free M with r=1 < f+2, every term B(T)A(T) nonzero, and Psi=0: {2,-2,3,-3,1/6,-1/6} (lambda=3,f=0); {2,-1/2} (lambda=0,f=2); {3,-3,1/9} (lambda=1,f=1); {2,-2,5,-5,1/100} (lambda=2,f=1). Exact, and agreed by both engines. All four are instances of clio-Q565-r1-closed-form at r=1, theta=(0), which gives Psi = 1 - (prod_t w_t)^{-2}: the zero locus there is exactly {prod_t w_t = +-1}, which has CODIMENSION 1 IN THE STRATUM and so is missed almost surely by random draws. Witness (a) sits in a cell the original 26/26 sweep actually visited (lambda=3,f=0,n=6,r=1=f+1) and reported as zero-free; nothing was wrong with the draws. Also settled: the stratum meets {prod w = +-1} iff f >= 1 or lambda >= 3, so the smallest counterexamples are exactly where they are.

A second, theta-INDEPENDENT mechanism: if f=0 (so M=-M) then B(-T)=B(T) and A(-T) = (-1)^{sum_j m_j + C(r,2)} A(T), so reindexing T -> -T gives Psi = (-1)^{sum_j m_j + C(r,2)} Psi, hence Psi=0 when sum_j m_j + C(r,2) is odd. Needs no parity hypothesis on m. Verified 140/140; control (f=0, sum+C(r,2) even, m mixed parity) nonzero 122/126 (t9_corrected.py). Strictly weaker than the main theorem where both apply, and they agree on the overlap.

INSTRUMENT FAULT, recorded because the control is what found it. I first wrote clio-Q576-f0-global-sign as A(-T) = (-1)^{C(r,2)} A(T), having silently carried over the fact that sum_j m_j is even for theta=(0,...,r-1) (where m_j=2(j-1)) -- true there, false in general. Run as a prediction for arbitrary theta it scored 26/60, i.e. about half, which is the signature of an unmodelled sign rather than of a wrong theorem. Inserting (-1)^{sum_j m_j} gives 140/140. LESSON: a sign specialised at the theta I had in mind read as a sign that was not there; a law checked only where its two forms agree is unchecked.

Below the threshold, r <= f+1-delta, Psi does NOT vanish identically on the stratum -- but this is COMPUTED, not proved: 0 zeros in 6 independent draws in each of the 41 cells with r <= f+1 of t2_grid.py (delta=0), plus the two green boundary controls of t11_sharp.py (280 draws). The core identity says nothing outside its two cases, and I have no proof that Z != 0 there, only measurements.
